precepts.text: Wickedness came from Babylon from ancient judges, who seemed to govern the people. Those elders brought Babylonian ideas home, the root of the Talmud and the traditions Christ condemned.
precepts.point: They have thrown down thine altars and slain thy prophets, and I, even I only, am left. Israel's rulers killed the prophets who taught against them. The same people mock the purple and gold today.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Who were the rulers who killed the prophets? The history of Susanna shows where their wickedness came from. “There dwelt a man in Babylon, called Joacim”, a great rich man with a fair garden, “and to him resorted the Jews; because he was more honourable than all others.” He was an elder, a leader, and the people came to sit with him.

“The same year were appointed two of the ancients of the people to be judges, such as the Lord spake of, that wickedness came from Babylon from ancient judges, who seemed to govern the people.” We had ancient judges in Babylon, and they brought Babylonian doctrine and ideals along with them. They seemed to govern the people, but they were not true governors; they were evil and wicked as hell.

These same elders who came out of Babylon, and whose line made its way down to the time of Roman rule, started the Talmud. The Babylonian Talmud: they got it from Babylon. So when Christ condemned their traditions, those traditions came from Babylon. These are the fathers of the Pharisees, the same spirit of the rulers who slew the prophets.

precepts.text: The Lord raised up the holy spirit of a young youth named Daniel; another example of the spirit put on a man at a very young age.
precepts.point: David was also young when the spirit came on him, and that is nothing new either; the Most High does not choose the ones everybody expects, for the spirit of Christ was in the prophets he selected.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
David was young when the spirit came on him. He was the youngest son, and “the Spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day forward.” That is nothing new either.

“Therefore when she was led to be put to death, the Lord raised up the holy spirit of a young youth whose name was Daniel”. Another example of the spirit put on a man at a very young age. The Most High does not choose the ones everybody expects.

moments.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

points: Back to Ecclesiasticus 9:8: love is kindled as a fire. To kindle is to blow on it. It starts as a little ember, and you keep nurturing it by entertaining the thoughts day in and day out, never turning your head, until it becomes inflamed. That's exactly what these two elders did at that man's house, and lust made two old judges into conspirators.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

points: The two elders saw her going in every day, and walking; so that their lust was inflamed toward her. And they perverted their own mind, and turned away their eyes, that they might not look unto heaven, nor remember just judgments.

They turned their eyes away from God. We just read: give me thine heart, turn your eyes this way. They said no, I'm going this way. Well, then that's your god. They would not remember judgment because they were inflamed; they were enticed, like James says, drawn away and enticed.
